title: The Underworld after the Armistice
summary: The dead from November 1918 to the eve of the 1929 crash.

claims.text: The setting runs from Armistice Day, 11 November 1918, until the eve of the 1929 stock market crash.
Charon still rules the Empire in theory, though no one has seen Charon in years.
Stygia has fallen to treachery, and the Dark Kingdom of Iron is close to collapse.
The Shadowlands and the heart of the Empire are all but cut off; each Necropolis is an island among enemies.

title: The Fourth Great Maelstrom
summary: The psychic storm born of the Somme.

claims.text: The carnage of the Somme spawned the Fourth Great Maelstrom, which still rages.
The storm lasts until the Shadow-eaten who make it up are beaten and the Nihils sealed.
A Maelstrom is a violent venting from the Tempest or Labyrinth into the Shadowlands, usually with Spectres.

title: The War of the Dead
summary: What wraiths mean by the Great War.

claims.text: Among wraiths the Great War means the Underworld conflict that follows the living one; the living war they call the War to End All Wars, or just the war.
Ghosts of tanks, zeppelins and planes, drones re-running doomed charges and drifting clouds of poison gas fill the Underworld.

title: The Insurrection
summary: The Grim Legion's grab for the Dark Empire.

claims.text: The Insurrection is the Grim Legion's attempt to take the Dark Empire of Iron.
Its supporters call themselves Imperialists of the New Stygian regime; opponents call them Insurrectionists.
A Loyalist is a wraith who opposes the Smiling Lord's forces in the Insurrection.
Grim Legion traitors may already be inside a Citadel's walls.

title: Black Mask and the Ministry of Intelligence
summary: The spy services of the Legions.

claims.text: The Black Mask is the Grim Legion's espionage order.
The Ministry of Intelligence is the Iron Legion's espionage order.
The Magisterium Veritatis is Stygia's secret police.

title: Orders of the Legions
summary: Some named orders and branches of the 1920s Legions.

claims.text: The Bleak Legion is no true Legion but a Russian branch of the Silent Legion.
The Cataphractoi are the heavy cavalry of the Legion of Fate.
The Penitent Legion's Flesh Corps fights with moliated Leviathans, as the Beast Corps uses barghests.

title: The Breathless Dead
summary: Stygia's name for the dead of the Spanish Flu.

claims.text: Stygians call victims of the Spanish Flu the Breathless Dead.

title: Other Deadlands
summary: The afterlives beyond Stygia drawn into the war.

claims.text: Souls of the Jade Empire, the Bush of Ghosts and the Indian afterlife are all caught up in the age.
The Bush of Ghosts is the African Deadlands, called the Dark Kingdom of Ivory in Stygia.
The Jade Kingdom is the Asian Deadlands; Yellow Springs is its term for China's Deadlands.
Some travellers brave the Maelstrom to go home, or find themselves captive in afterlives not their own.

title: Words of the Far Deadlands
summary: Terms from the Jade Kingdom, the Bush of Ghosts and Swar.

claims.text: In the Jade Kingdom, hun is the half of a wraith's soul that is intellect and spirit, the Psyche; a kuei is a malevolent spirit ruled by its p'o.
In the Bush of Ghosts an ibambo is an African wraith, and a moriman is a spirit doctor who practises the Behest Arcanos.
Stygians call the Arcanos practised by the Tvashtriya Displace.
Yama is held to be lord of the Dead and judge of souls in the Indian afterlife.
The Generals of Oblivion are a select group of Nephwracks who serve Oblivion directly and side with or against Malfeans as they choose.
The Mutile is a common Spectre, called a Mortwight in the European Deadlands.
Johnny Songbirds are itinerant Chanteurs.
